content:
morgan: heads-up — CompetitorX shipped a low-cost embeddings tier this morning. getting inbound from sales.

sam: saw it. their price is aggressive. customers already asking if we can match.

jia: ACME pilot reached out. their priority is consistent recall + predictable latency, not lowest cost.

anika: thinking: ship an opt-in parity "lite vector" tier (quantized, lower-dim) as a tactical response, then plan Q3 work for real differentiators (quality tiers, reranker hooks).

tyler: quick check: runtime needs quantized kernels + small adjustments to batching and KV behavior. rough estimate: 3 dev-days for kernels, 2 for verification.

morgan: minimal MVP — what are the absolute must-haves?

sam: minimal: feature flag, model alias (e.g. embed-lite-v1), billing SKU, and a console opt-in toggle. docs note about quality.

jia: must gate with evals: require cosine recall >= 0.90 vs baseline on our eval set. ACME's acceptance is 0.88, so that gives us a margin.

anika: draft launch criteria:
- canary at 10% traffic for 48h
- p50 latency delta < +10ms, p95 < +40ms
- unit cost down >= 25%
- eval recall >= 0.90
- docs + billing mapping done
- ACME acceptance smoke test

tyler: runtime detail — prefix/KV cache with quantized weights might need a fallback path. fallback perf hit estimated <5% if we keep cache semantics.

morgan: make it opt-in only so default behavior doesn't change and customers don't accidentally get lower quality.

sam: agree. Q2 release: opt-in parity-lite. deferring tiered-quality/per-route selection to Q3.

jia: dependency checklist for tracker:
- eng-runtime: quantized kernel + cache fallback (owner: tyler)
- billing: SKU and pricing map (owner: lev)
- console: opt-in toggle + policy dropdown (owner: maya)
- docs: launch notes + caveats (owner: anika)

lev: noted. need SKU name and two price anchors by EOD Wed to sync with finance.

morgan: owners assigned: tyler (runtime), maya (console), lev (billing), anika (docs/comms), sam (release plan).

sam: timeline suggestion: spike/prototype by 2024-04-03, staging canary 2024-04-10, GA opt-in 2024-04-17.

tyler: realistic timeline: spike 2d, kernel work 3d, integration 2d, QA 2d = ~9 working days. might slide to late April unless parallelized.

anika: we can parallelize billing and console. prioritize runtime + billing first to unblock others.

morgan: comms plan: brief sales + CS with talking points, mark as Beta and list limitations (not for high-accuracy use cases). @lev prepare price anchors.

lev: will produce two anchor sets and threshold discounts. need margin floor input from finance.

jia: ACME acceptance: I'll run their sample corpus for recall/latency and report back.

sam: risks called out:
- customers assume parity tier equals default -> quality surprises
- telemetry may not capture multi-tenant cost correctly
- perf cliffs on specific sequence lengths

morgan: mitigations: opt-in only, enforce telemetry tagging on billing flow, include FAQ in launch notes.

anika: decision: proceed with opt-in parity-lite for Q2 as a stopgap, follow-up with Q3 quality-tier work. action items captured.

morgan: I'll post a short summary to #product and loop in sales ops. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: scheduled staging deploy `embed-lite-spike` for 2024-04-09 09:30 UTC

maya: console PR ready, waiting on billing SKU and price.

lev: targeting EOD Wed for anchors; will drop spreadsheets in the sales drive.

sam: next sync Friday 10am to review spike metrics. call out any blockers beforehand.

morgan: thanks all — cc: @tyler @maya @lev @anika @jia @sam
